name: Orchid purple
lede: Orchid purple is a bright, light purple built directly on [[orchid]], and it shares its exact screen color with a second library name, Amparo Purple.

sections.title: A family word's purple
sections.body:
The library marks Orchid purple as a direct modifier of the family word [[orchid]], recorded by Ridgway in 1912 [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists classify it as a vivid reddish purple, brighter and more saturated than most flower-named purples in our library [1]. At this hex our library also records a second name, Amparo Purple, at an identical value, two separate dictionary entries for one color [1].

The nearest distinct neighbor is [[light-hortense-violet|Light Hortense Violet]], about 2.7 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[floral-lavender|Lavender (Floral)]] not far behind [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 59, chroma 53, hue 320 degrees, Munsell 6.0P 5.8/12.4 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Orchid purple is not a painter's color. No painting in our archive of 23,781, as photographed, has a color within a small distance of this swatch covering even five percent of the canvas [2]. That describes our own archive, not painting as a whole, and the gap likely owes something to how rare a pigment this bright and this purple was before modern synthetic dyes [2].

origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature (1912); ColorHub library
